source.title: HDBSCAN is Surprisingly Effective at Finding Interpretable Clusters of the SAE Decoder Matrix

record.tranche_reason: The post applies clustering to SAE decoder features from GPT-2 Small and Gemma-2B, extending evidence about feature structure to language-model representations.
record.gate_note: The post reports the fraction of features classified as noise and gives several interpreted feature clusters. Layer-block similarities in UMAPs are recorded as a related finding, not as a test of the listed versions. Comparisons with k-means and agglomerative clustering are mentioned only as having mixed results, without reported measurements.
record.test_reason: The post takes SAE features of GPT-2 Small and Gemma-2-2B as given, as the output of disentangling superposition. It then reports how well its own method (HDBSCAN on decoder vectors) performs: noise fractions and examples of interpretable clusters. None of its results bear on whether toy-model superposition, the capacity account, polysemanticity without capacity pressure, SAE recovery of model features, SAE canonicity or 1-D features hold. The day-of-week PCA non-linearity and the 'Bug 2' remark touch on V6 and V5. Both are qualitative, not quantified, and the first is framed as reproducing Engels et al.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that the decoder matrix alone can reveal some feature families. HDBSCAN labels most features as noise and misses clusters. Clusters may be a better unit for auto-interpretability and steering. They also frame clusters as 'reverse feature splitting': multiple SAE latents standing in for one feature, such as Bricken's Bug 2. The Čech-complex guardrail is proposed future work, with no results.
record.recipe_differences: Uses cosine-based HDBSCAN clustering and UMAP visualization of SAE decoder vectors from GPT-2 Small and Gemma-2B; it does not reproduce the original toy-network setup or its interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported noise fraction depends on clustering hyperparameters; the post notes that even GPT2-Small's last layer can have a high noise fraction depending on those choices.

fits_no_version.finding: HDBSCAN on cosine distances of SAE decoder vectors leaves most latents as noise (>90% in Gemma-2-2B; at best ~35% clustered in GPT-2 Small layer 4). The clusters it does find group semantically related latents (cardinal directions, 'side', 'points', days of week, cooking).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cosine-similarity clustering of SAE decoder directions recovers some interpretable feature families, but leaves most latents unclustered.

fits_no_version.finding: A 2D PCA of the day-of-week cluster's decoder vectors reportedly shows the same non-linear (circular) structure as Engels et al. It is shown as a figure only, with no quantification.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some SAE latent families form multi-dimensional, non-linear structures (bears on V6 only qualitatively).

fits_no_version.finding: Qualitative UMAP layouts of clustered latents look similar within blocks of layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE decoder-space cluster layouts can show qualitative similarities across groups of layers.

record.problems: The post says most features are classified as noise and acknowledges that HDBSCAN does not find all clusters. Cluster interpretations are partly based on GPT-4o-Mini responses and examples rather than a stated quantitative validation; cluster 435 includes listed features that do not match the authors' main interpretation. The post is informal and says code and clustered features are not yet open-sourced.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant result rows were omitted. The post's proposed Čech-complex guardrailing and filtration are future work, not reported results.

untested.parts: Toy networks, sparsity-dependent transition, near-orthogonal geometry: not studied.
Capacity pressure as the cause of polysemanticity: not studied.
Polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure: not studied.
Whether real models spread features across neurons, or whether SAEs recover sparse model features: assumed, not measured.
Completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features: only argued informally via 'reverse feature splitting' and Bug 2, not measured.
Whether superposed features are 1-D: only a qualitative PCA of a day-of-week cluster, with no quantitative test.

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal LessWrong post with no controls, no uncertainty, no code and no quantitative validation of cluster interpretations, which rely on GPT-4o-Mini autointerp and examples. The reader's T3/V4 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels were dropped: the results are the performance and outputs of the authors' own clustering method applied to assumed SAE features. The k-means and agglomerative comparisons are mentioned only in comments, without data.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks, feature overlap or near-orthogonality, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular superposition geometry.
Does not test whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure or whether it evidences superposition.
Tests interpreted SAE feature clusters in GPT-2 Small and Gemma-2B, but not feature spreading across neurons, feature sparsity directly, or SAE recovery comprehensively.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not test whether the represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: GEMMA-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: HDBSCAN clustering of SAE decoder vectors; measured features assigned to noise
rows.measure: Percentage of features classified as noise
rows.note: The post states this applies across all Gemma-2-2B layers; most features were not assigned to clusters.
rows.check: The noise fraction measures HDBSCAN's clustering coverage, which is the study's own method performance. It is not a measure of features spread across neurons or of SAE recovery, so it should not link to V4. The 'partial' state has no meaning against the claim.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: HDBSCAN clustering of SAE decoder vectors; measured features assigned to clusters
rows.measure: Percentage of features classified into clusters
rows.note: The post says this is the best result and occurs at a single layer.
rows.check: The ~35% clustered at GPT-2 layer 4 is method performance and depends on hyperparameters. It does not bear on V4.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: HDBSCAN clustering of SAE decoder vectors; measured features assigned to noise
rows.measure: Percentage of features classified as noise
rows.note: The text says the last layer can also have a high noise fraction depending on hyperparameters, but gives no value for that condition.
rows.check: Method performance with no value given, and it is hyperparameter-dependent. Not a claim measure.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: HDBSCAN cluster of SAE decoder vectors interpreted using feature activations and GPT-4o-Mini responses
rows.value: Features were interpreted as cardinal directions, including North, South, East, West, and Northeast
rows.note: The post gives example activations and interpretations for features in the cluster; GPT-4o-Mini responses are shown explicitly for North features.
rows.check: This shows the clustering method groups related SAE latents (cardinal directions). It assumes the SAE features rather than testing whether SAEs recover the model's features. The authors use it as an example of Bricken 'Bug 2', multiple latents for one feature.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: HDBSCAN cluster of SAE decoder vectors interpreted using feature activations and GPT-4o-Mini responses
rows.value: The post describes the features as different uses of the word “side” and its variations
rows.note: The feature list in the prose is [489, 6868, 7801, 19879, 20215], while the table starts with feature 498; the discrepancy is not resolved in the text.
rows.check: A cluster-interpretability example for the study's own method. The listed feature id (489) and table id (498) are inconsistent. The 4o-Mini explanation for 7801 (dominance/control) does not fit 'side'.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: HDBSCAN cluster of SAE decoder vectors interpreted from feature activations
rows.value: Features relate to different days of the week, plus one feature for “Yesterday”
rows.note: The post also reports a 2D PCA of these features, but gives no numerical result for it.
rows.check: A cluster-interpretability example for the study's own method. The accompanying 2D PCA non-linearity bears only qualitatively on V6 and is recorded under fits_no_version.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: HDBSCAN cluster of SAE decoder vectors interpreted using feature activations and GPT-4o-Mini responses
rows.value: The authors describe the cluster as primarily related to cooking processes and ingredients, while listed features also concern spatial relations, punctuation, and numerical values
rows.note: The post itself notes that individual features may not seem connected and that human review can be needed.
rows.check: A cluster-interpretability example for the study's own method. Several members (punctuation, numbers, spatial) do not match the stated cooking theme.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: HDBSCAN cluster of SAE decoder vectors interpreted from feature activations
rows.value: The post says the cluster activates on different meanings of “points,” including percentage, score, or direction
rows.note: No feature list or additional measurements are provided.
rows.check: A one-sentence mention with no features or data. It is a method example, not a claim measure.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Compared 2D UMAP cluster layouts across layers
rows.measure: Qualitative similarity of UMAP cluster layouts across layers
rows.value: Layers 1–3 look similar, as do layers 4–6; layers 7–9 may also be similar
rows.note: This is a reported SAE decoder-space pattern, but it does not test any listed claim version.

rows.subject: GEMMA-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared 2D UMAP cluster layouts across layers
rows.measure: Qualitative similarity of UMAP cluster layouts across layers
rows.value: Layers 4–5, 11–14, and 19–22 look similar within their respective groups
rows.note: The post says this pattern appears despite clustering only ~10% of features; the layer-block pattern itself does not test a listed claim version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Several clusters have reported coherent semantic or temporal interpretations, providing examples of SAE features grouped into interpretable families (r4, r5, r6, r8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: HDBSCAN classifies >90% of Gemma features as noise and clusters at best ~35% for one GPT2-Small layer; one interpreted cluster also contains features the authors describe as unrelated (r1, r2, r7).
